## User Story

As a maintainer whose approved branch picked up trunk before merging
I want to still reach a delivery receipt after the pull-request head advances past the accepted SHA
So that a landed, verified deliverable can be closed instead of becoming permanently unclosable

## Scope

Prove externally performed multi-commit squash delivery without weakening exact-head delivery authority.

When a pull request is merged outside the governed `deliver` provider action — for example squash-merged by a maintainer in the GitHub UI — the delivery verifier must still be able to prove, from evidence alone, that the merge was a squash of the accepted head. Today it can only do so when the pull request contained exactly one non-merge source commit (`provesSingleSourceSquash`, `scripts/task-tracker/lib/delivery-verification.mjs`). Every multi-commit externally squash-merged pull request reaches `delivery-verification:merge-method-unknown` and can never obtain a receipt, so its issue can never close.

GitHub supplies no authoritative historical merge method. Verified live against PR #1489: the REST payload exposes `merged`, `merged_by`, `merge_commit_sha`, `mergeable`, `mergeable_state`, and `auto_merge`, none of which records the method used; `rebaseable` and `squash_merge_commit_title` are both null after merge. The production adapter correspondingly never populates `pullRequest.mergeMethod`, so `mergeMethodObservation` is always null on this path. A complete topology proof is therefore required rather than preferred.

In scope: a multi-source squash proof at the evidence-verification boundary that binds the complete pull-request source inventory to the accepted head, proves the merged tree is exactly the accepted tree, and fails closed on any incomplete or ambiguous evidence.

Out of scope for this issue: general post-approval head-advance recovery. The earlier framing of this issue claimed such an advance "permanently orphans" delivery. That was wrong on both counts — the immediate blocker is the multi-commit squash proof, and re-verification demonstrably realigns the accepted SHA (done live on #1488, realigned to 82eba885). No head-advance recovery will be added unless a separate failing test proves it is required to close #1485 or #1488.

### Amended scope — reopened-close terminal recovery

Delivering this issue's own attribution repair required reopening #1490 after it had
already been delivered and closed at accepted SHA `d6a3dece`. The completed
`aitm.delivered-close/v1` transaction `ad96d1e1-8c17-471e-a060-279975761e50` survived the
reopen with all eight steps recorded, so `close` now refuses with
`close-convergence:terminal-state-conflict`: a record asserting the issue was closed
contradicts an open issue.

That transaction records a true historical delivery and must not be hand-retired. The
existing supersession mechanism (#1466) deliberately does not cover this shape: its
restart path accepts at most three completed steps and requires a null disposition with a
ToDo/BLOCKED label, because it is built for a close interrupted PARTWAY, not one that ran
to completion and was later reopened.

In scope: one narrowly bounded, fail-closed recovery mode behind an explicit new flag,
`npx aitm close <N> --restart-reopened-transaction`, that authorizes only the complete
eight-step-completed / reopened / Review / Delivered shape, writes durable read-back
verified supersession evidence before replacing the active marker, and then runs the
normal eight-step close saga from a fresh transaction with no completed steps.

Out of scope: weakening or broadening `--restart-stale-transaction`, relaxing the generic
issue-body marker protection, and any change to `--force`, `--repair`, or
disposition-close flags, with which the new flag is incompatible.
## Reproduction

1. Drive any issue to Review with an exact-head Test receipt and recorded review approval. Note the accepted SHA.
2. Open a pull request from that branch containing more than one commit.
3. Squash-merge it in the GitHub UI, outside the governed `deliver` provider action.
4. Run `npx aitm deliver #N`. Observe `delivery-verification:merge-method-unknown`.
5. Run `npx aitm close #N`. Observe the inherited refusal; the issue cannot close.

Observed live on #1488 at accepted head `82eba885bac295a57c236c611c84e0fd6f69d7e3`, squash-merged as `3a044ea8411a9f0e34f54c33f412749cb735c457` via PR #1489 (3 source commits). #1485 is in the same condition at accepted head `94575a4a009383c8749343c5c8023241c84ebd5c`, squash-merged as `f83eb22f6e60c26235da479c054edbdb3ee0755b` via PR #1487 (5 source commits).

Both merged trees are byte-identical to their accepted heads, and required CI passed for both pull requests. The deliverables are correct and landed; only the receipt proof is missing.

## Root Cause

`classifyMergeMethod` (`scripts/task-tracker/lib/delivery-verification.mjs`) returns `rewritten-one-parent` for any squash: one parent, and the merge SHA differs from the accepted head. `verifyLiveDelivery` then has to resolve that into a concrete method. For an externally merged pull request `requireAuthorizedBytes` is false and `mergeMethodObservation` is null, so the only remaining path is `provesSingleSourceSquash`.

That proof requires the pull request to contain exactly one source commit, and that commit to have exactly one parent:

- `inventory.length !== 1` returns false
- `source.parents.length === 1` is required

Any multi-commit pull request fails the first condition, and a pull request whose head is itself a merge commit also fails the second. The classification collapses to `unknown` and `verifyLiveDelivery` throws `delivery-verification:merge-method-unknown`. `close` inherits the refusal because it resolves the same delivery authority.

Observed live on both blocked issues:

| | PR #1487 (#1485) | PR #1489 (#1488) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| accepted head | `94575a4a` | `82eba885` (a merge commit) |
| source commits | 5 | 3 |
| merge commit | `f83eb22f` | `3a044ea8` |
| parents of merge commit | 1 (`e5b3060c`) | 1 (`f83eb22f`) |
| tree(merge) vs tree(accepted) | identical `d23b0244` | identical `0c2d4548` |
| parent is ancestor of accepted head | yes | yes |

The evidence needed for a complete proof is present in both cases; the verifier simply has no rule that consumes it.

## Fix Direction

Add a multi-source squash proof beside `provesSingleSourceSquash` and consult it from the `rewritten-one-parent` branch of `verifyLiveDelivery`. Implement it as a separate function rather than by extending `classifyMergeMethod`, so that classifier stays pure and synchronous and the new proof is independently testable.

The proof is conjunctive; every condition must hold:

1. the merge commit has exactly one parent;
2. the merge SHA differs from the accepted SHA;
3. the merge commit tree equals the accepted head tree;
4. the merge commit parent is an ancestor of the accepted head;
5. the source inventory is complete, non-empty, and its recorded head equals the accepted SHA;
6. the merge commit is reachable from the resolved base ref (already enforced upstream).

Why it cannot misclassify. An ordinary merge has two parents and fails (1); it is already classified as `merge` before reaching this branch. A multi-commit rebase replays commits onto the base, so the merge SHA is the last replayed commit and its parent is a newly created rewrite that never existed on the source branch, failing (4) — this is the condition that discriminates rebase. A fast-forward fails (2). A squash that dropped or reverted accepted content changes the tree and fails (3), which is also what rejects a descendant that reverted accepted content. Incomplete evidence fails (5).

Deliberately not relied upon: repository merge settings, merge commit title or message, one-parent topology alone, tree equality alone, and accepted-SHA reachability alone. Conditions 1, 3, and 4 are individually insufficient and sound only in conjunction.

Known imprecision, accepted deliberately: a single-commit rebase is topologically identical to a single-commit squash — one commit, same tree, parent is the base tip — and no local or GitHub evidence distinguishes them. The two outcomes are semantically identical. Such a merge is classified as a squash.

Known fail-closed edge: condition (4) refuses a legitimate squash of a branch that was never synced with a base that had moved, because the merge parent would then not be an ancestor of the accepted head. This refuses rather than misclassifies.

Do not weaken `delivery-preflight`, approval, exact-head, or receipt requirements. The fix belongs strictly at the evidence-verification boundary.

## Out of Scope

- Weakening or removing the exact-head evidence contract.
- Accepting a delivery receipt for content that was never verified.
- Auto-closing an issue that has no receipt at all.
- Treating plain ancestry as sufficient, without proving the approved content is still included in the advanced head.
- Changing the #1488 bind-timer repair or #1485's merge-back branch-authority repair.

## Story Origin

- **kind**: code
- **discovered-during**: #1488
- **discovery-context**: trunk was merged into #1488's branch after review approval to pick up #1485; the pull-request head advanced off the accepted SHA, and after the merge `deliver` and `close` both refused `ambiguous-pr` with no reachable recovery
- **scope-boundary**: delivery-authority evidence selection; independent of the #1488 bind-timer repair and of #1485's merge-back branch-authority repair

## Plan Metadata

- **Governing-analysis**: deep-dive analysis section on this issue (mirrored from comment 5515675443)
- **Approach**: conjunctive six-condition topology proof for an externally squash-merged multi-commit pull request, implemented as a separate predicate beside `provesSingleSourceSquash`
- **Discriminator**: the merge parent must be an ancestor of the accepted head; a rebase parent is a newly created rewrite and fails this, which is what separates squash from rebase
- **Change surface**: one production file, `scripts/task-tracker/lib/delivery-verification.mjs`. No adapter change is needed — source evidence already carries per-commit trees and `inspectMergeCommit` already returns the merge tree and parents
- **Safety**: `delivery-preflight`, approval, exact-head, and receipt requirements are untouched; the fix lives strictly at the evidence-verification boundary
- **Compatibility**: existing single-source external-squash, provider-action, current-head, and historical-intent recovery paths keep their present behavior
- **Accepted imprecision**: a single-commit rebase is topologically identical to a single-commit squash and is classified as a squash; the outcomes are semantically identical
- **Accepted fail-closed edge**: a legitimate squash of a branch never synced with a moved base is refused, not misclassified
- **Test hazard**: the existing `liveInput` fixture sets `pullRequest.mergeMethod`, which short-circuits the proof; new cases must omit it or they will not exercise the new code
- **Execution**: serial execution in the recorded #1490 worktree cut from trunk; no parallel agents
- **Delivery discipline**: deliver through the governed provider flow so the delivery intent exists before the provider action; do not repeat the manual-merge-without-intent condition
- **Blocked consumers**: #1485 and #1488 cannot obtain delivery receipts or close until this lands; #1226 and the remaining #1220 chain sit behind them

## Deep-Dive Analysis (2026-09-02)

> Mirrored from comment #issuecomment-5515675443 (https://github.com/kburson/ai-task-manager/issues/1490#issuecomment-5515675443). Comment is the diff-history canonical; this body copy is the gate-canonical source.

### Files to edit

- `scripts/task-tracker/lib/delivery-verification.mjs` — add a multi-source squash proof beside `provesSingleSourceSquash` and consult it from the `rewritten-one-parent` branch of `verifyLiveDelivery`.
- `scripts/tests/unit/task-tracker/lib/delivery-verification-attribution.test.mjs` — extend with the topology cases, or add a focused sibling test file if the fixture surface grows too large for that file's current shape.

Correction to the approved checkpoint plan: **no change to `scripts/task-tracker/verbs/deliver.mjs` is required.** The checkpoint assumed the accepted head tree and an ancestry call would have to be threaded in. Reading the adapter proved otherwise:

- `fetchCompletePullRequestCommits` already requests `tree{oid}` for every source commit, so `pullRequest.sourceCommitEvidence` carries `{message, oid, parents, tree}` per commit. The accepted head tree is the entry whose `oid` equals the accepted SHA.
- `inspectMergeCommit` delegates to `inspectCommitObject`, which returns `{parents, tree, commitTitle, commitMessage}`.
- `input.isAncestor` is already a required verification function.

All six proof inputs are therefore already present at the verification boundary. The change surface is one production file.

### The proof

Implemented as a separate predicate, not by extending `classifyMergeMethod`. That classifier stays pure and synchronous; the new proof is async only because ancestry resolution is. Conjunctive — every condition must hold, and any missing or malformed evidence returns false rather than throwing:

1. the merge commit has exactly one parent;
2. the merge SHA differs from the accepted SHA;
3. the merge commit tree equals the accepted head tree, taken from the source evidence entry whose oid is the accepted SHA;
4. the merge commit parent is an ancestor of the accepted SHA;
5. the source inventory is complete, non-empty, and its recorded head equals the accepted SHA;
6. the merge commit is reachable from the resolved base ref, already enforced upstream in `verifyLiveDelivery` before this point.

Condition 4 is the one doing the discriminating work, and it is the reason this cannot be satisfied by a rebase.

### Why each wrong classification is excluded

An ordinary merge carries two parents with `parents[1]` equal to the accepted head, so `classifyMergeMethod` returns `merge` and never reaches this branch; it also fails condition 1.

A multi-commit rebase replays each source commit onto the base. The merge SHA is the last replayed commit, and its parent is the newly created rewrite of the previous source commit. That object never existed on the source branch, so it cannot be an ancestor of the accepted head, and condition 4 fails.

A fast-forward leaves the merge SHA equal to the accepted SHA and fails condition 2.

A squash that dropped, altered, or reverted accepted content produces a different tree and fails condition 3. This is also what rejects a descendant commit that reverted the approved change: a revert necessarily changes the tree.

Incomplete or unbound source evidence fails condition 5.

Deliberately not relied upon, each individually insufficient: repository merge settings, merge commit title or message, one-parent topology alone, tree equality alone, and accepted-SHA reachability alone.

### Two accepted imprecisions

A single-commit rebase is topologically indistinguishable from a single-commit squash — one commit, identical tree, parent is the base tip — and no local or GitHub evidence separates them. The outcomes are semantically identical. Such a merge is classified as a squash. This is recorded rather than hidden.

Condition 4 fail-closes on a legitimate squash of a branch that was never synced with a base that had moved on, because the merge parent would then not be an ancestor of the accepted head. That refuses rather than misclassifies, which is the correct direction, but it will surprise someone eventually.

### Step-by-step implementation plan

1. Add failing tests reproducing PR #1487's shape: five ordinary source commits, a one-parent rewritten merge commit, merge tree equal to the accepted head tree, merge parent an ancestor of the accepted head. Expect a squash classification.
2. Add failing tests reproducing PR #1489's shape, where the accepted head is itself a merge commit with two parents. Expect a squash classification, proving the proof does not require the accepted head to be a simple commit.
3. Add failing negative tests: multi-commit rebase topology, ordinary two-parent merge, fast-forward, tree mismatch, reverted descendant, and incomplete source inventory.
4. Observe all of the above fail against the current verifier.
5. Implement the predicate and wire it into the `rewritten-one-parent` branch alongside the existing single-source proof, preserving the existing precedence so nothing that resolves today changes.
6. Confirm the existing single-source external-squash, provider-action, current-head, and historical-intent paths remain green.
7. Verify against the two real pull requests using their recorded topology as fixture data.

### Test additions

- `scripts/tests/unit/task-tracker/lib/delivery-verification-attribution.test.mjs` — multi-commit external squash accepted for both real pull-request shapes; rebase, ordinary merge, fast-forward, tree mismatch, reverted descendant, and incomplete inventory each refused; existing recovery paths unchanged.

Note for fixture accuracy: the existing `liveInput` helper sets `pullRequest.mergeMethod: 'squash'`, which short-circuits the proof through `mergeMethodObservation`. The production adapter never sets that field. New tests must omit it, or they will pass without exercising the new code at all.

### Identified risks

The largest risk is a test that appears to prove the new path but actually passes through the existing `mergeMethodObservation` short-circuit. Every new case must leave `mergeMethod` unset on the pull-request fixture.

A second risk is weakening the existing single-source proof while adding the multi-source one. The two must remain independent, with the existing one unchanged and still covered.

A third risk is treating tree equality as sufficient on its own. It is not: a rebase produces the same final tree. Conditions 1 through 5 are sound only in conjunction, and the tests must include a case where tree equality holds but ancestry does not.

### Sibling sub-issues to spawn

None.

## Definition of Done
<!--
Each item below MUST be individually verified by running the declared
verifier. Do not bulk-check. Do not preemptively check. The visible checkbox
is the sign-off; the hidden `aitm-dod-evidence:<key>` marker is the evidence
trail. `/task check` refuses to tick a stampable Functional DoD item without
its marker; run `/task dod-stamp <key>` to produce one. The two derived keys
(`acs`, `checkboxes`) are auto-stamped by `/task close` from the body itself.
See `skill/shared/rules/functional-dod.md` for the full contract.

Lifecycle items are verified during Review. Housekeeping items are finalized
during Close; their separate headings make the owning workflow phase explicit.

Kind-aware items (#681): append a `dod:kinds` HTML-comment annotation to scope
an item to a set of issue kinds. `exclude="spike,research"` renders the item for
every kind EXCEPT those listed; `include="code"` renders it only for the listed
kinds; an item with no annotation applies to every kind (the default). The
`tests` item is excluded for the no-code kinds `spike` and `research`, which ship
findings rather than code and would otherwise carry a test-suite DoD item and a
`npm run test:all` verification command they can never satisfy. Filtering happens
at render time in `preflight-issue.mjs`; a filtered-out item is simply absent, so
no phantom evidence marker is ever required for it.

Diff-decides for `docs-only` (#865): the `tests` item deliberately does NOT
static-exclude `docs-only`. A `docs-only` issue can quietly touch code, so the
kind alone must not launder it out of the suite. Instead the `tests` item is
dropped only when the render is `--kind docs-only` AND a supplied
`--changed-paths-file` proves the `trunk...HEAD` diff is documentation-only
(default-deny: any unclassified/empty/mixed diff keeps the item). "The kind
declares, the diff decides."
-->
